deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a German prose page from a history notebook, folio 43. It continues the previous page's narrative of the Persian Wars and runs on into the next page.

Content in order:
(1) The end of Thermopylae: Leonidas is surrounded, there is a furious fight, and all the Spartans fall except one.
(2) Xerxes takes Athens and burns it.
(3) An indecisive naval battle at Cape Artemisium, after which the Greeks withdraw into the bay of Salamis.
(4) The battle of Salamis, which the Greeks win, dated here '23 September 480'.
(5) Xerxes returns to Asia and leaves Mardonius in Macedonia with 300000 men; the first digit is lost or obscured at the edge.
(6) In 479 the campaign is renewed. The Greeks are better allied, and the battle of Plataea decides the war; Mardonius is killed.
(7) On the same day the Greek fleet defeats the Persian fleet at Cape Mycale.
(8) The wars continue for about 30 more years, but now the Greeks are the attackers.

There are no formulas, computations or derivations to reconstruct. The hand, spelling and content (a dictated or schoolroom world-history summary) suggest lecture or school notes. They may not be in Gauss's own hand. They seem to be bound into the 'HB.Lagrange1816' bundle by accident or for archival reasons.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: the page places Artemisium 'on the same day' as the burning of Athens. In fact Artemisium was fought at the same time as Thermopylae, and Athens was burned some days later.
The date '23 September 480' for Salamis is one of several traditional dates. Modern estimates are usually late September (c. 22–29 Sept.) 480 BC; the precise day is uncertain.
The figure of 300000 men for Mardonius follows Herodotus and is regarded by modern historians as greatly exaggerated.
'30 Jahre' of further war (to the Peace of Callias, 449) is a rounding; 479 to 449 is 30 years, which is consistent.

transcription_corrections: The folio number '43' is at the top right corner; the small mark after 'Spartaner' at the top left is a separate marker ('3'?), not part of the text.
'ungleich schwerere[?] Weise' is more likely 'ungleich besserer Weise' ('auf eine ungleich bessere Weise als der vorige'), which fits the next sentence about the Greeks being better allied.
'{+mit+} 300000' — in the image the inserted 'mit' stands over a number whose first digit is at the very left edge, so it reads like '00000'. 300000 is the historically expected (Herodotean) figure.

The interlinear insertion above 'selbigen Tage' is very faint. 'einen Angriff über' is uncertain, and the main-line verb before 'die griechische Flotte' may not be 'schlug' (it possibly reads 'verfolgt' or similar).
'zwar[?] einer[?] mit den persischen Angriffen verschont' is uncertain; the image may read '... nicht immer mit den persischen Angriffen verschont'.
